headline: Highest risk is data leakage from social-auto-upload’s broad network egress if paired with document-processing outputs; other pairwise risks are mostly low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, browser, or stdin/stdout bridge, so it cannot ingest social-auto-upload’s outputs by default. social-auto-upload is CLI/headless and exposes files/APIs, but without a shared channel the pairwise prompt-injection path is blocked.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies social-auto-upload output into Pathway inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid manual copy-paste between outputs and inputs.
Do not add a shared MCP server or queue.
Review any future bridge for provenance tagging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway touches no data classes and has no egress, but social-auto-upload has broad network egress and handles account data plus media files. If Pathway outputs sensitive document content that is then fed into social-auto-upload, the pair can leak that content through uploads or API calls; the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Pathway processes sensitive documents and its outputs are passed into social-auto-upload inputs, leakage is possible.
IF social-auto-upload uploads content derived from Pathway outputs to external platforms, exfiltration occurs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of the upload pipeline.
Use a redaction step before any handoff.
Restrict social-auto-upload to non-sensitive media.
Disable or firewall outbound uploads during testing.
Separate credentials and accounts per workflow.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are effectively write-limited: Pathway cannot write files or modify git, and social-auto-upload also cannot write files or modify git. The only overlap is broad network egress on B, so there is no shared mutable resource conflict in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF both are wrapped by an orchestrator that adds shared mutable state, contention may appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Use separate working directories.
Avoid shared git repositories.
Add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing agent, so its outputs can be treated as facts by downstream automation. social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader with API calls and account data, so if it consumes Pathway output without verification, incorrect document-derived instructions can cascade into wrong uploads or account actions.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses Pathway output as authoritative input, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Pathway produces malformed metadata and B uploads it without validation, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents.
Require human review for upload targets.
Compare Pathway output against source documents.
Reject outputs missing required fields.
Log and quarantine failed handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Pathway’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency controls, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media with broad egress to external platforms. Because residency, retention, and certification details are undocumented for both, the safest reading is a compliance mismatch risk rather than none; uncertainty escalates above low.
conditions: IF Pathway processes regulated documents and social-auto-upload transmits derived data to external services, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF either agent is used with EU PII or PHI, residency and certification gaps become material.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Block regulated data from the upload path.
Confirm residency and retention settings.
Use separate tenants for regulated workflows.
Document a DPA or equivalent before deployment.
